rules.description: Structural PK parameters must be finite and strictly positive (> 0)
rules.scientific_rationale: Clearances, compartmental volumes, rate constants, and half-lives represent physical rates, capacities, or timescales and must be strictly positive finite real numbers in standard compartmental pharmacokinetic parameterizations.
rules.recommendation: Reject non-positive, zero, NaN, or infinite structural parameter estimates; inspect estimation boundary constraints and log-transformation.
rules.reference_basis: Mathematical domain identity for compartmental pharmacokinetic differential equations. Regulatory reporting context: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) & Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER), Population Pharmacokinetics: Guidance for Industry (Silver Spring, MD: FDA; February 2022); European Medicines Agency (EMA), Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP), Guideline on Reporting the Results of Population Pharmacokinetic Analyses, Doc. Ref. CHMP/EWP/185990/06 (London, UK: EMA; June 2007).

rules.description: Parameter units must be explicitly provided, dimensionally compatible, and canonically unique
rules.scientific_rationale: Pharmacokinetic parameters require explicit physical dimensions (volume/time for clearance, volume for compartments, inverse time for rate constants, dimensionless fraction/percent for bioavailability, time for half-life) and unique canonical assignment.
rules.recommendation: Provide explicit dimensionally compatible units for every parameter and remove duplicate or conflicting parameter aliases.
rules.reference_basis: Dimensional analysis identity (SI / clinical pharmacokinetic unit conversion factors: 1 L = 1000 mL, 1 h = 60 min, 1 day = 24 h) and PharmAgent canonical parameter uniqueness rule (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Absolute bioavailability fraction F must lie in (0, 1] (or (0%, 100%])
rules.scientific_rationale: Absolute systemic bioavailability F represents the fraction of an administered dose reaching the systemic circulation unchanged and is bounded by conservation of mass on (0, 1]. Relative bioavailability between two formulations can exceed 1.0 only with documented justification.
rules.recommendation: Verify whether F represents absolute bioavailability (must be <= 1.0) or relative bioavailability against a lower-exposure reference formulation.
rules.reference_basis: Conservation of mass identity for absolute bioavailability fraction (0 < F <= 1). Relative bioavailability override convention: PharmAgent screening rule (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Systemic hepatic blood clearance (CL_blood) compared against reference adult hepatic blood flow (Q_H) and cardiac output (CO) when hepatic elimination applies
rules.scientific_rationale: For small-molecule or peptide drugs cleared primarily by the liver, whole-blood hepatic clearance (CL_blood = CL_plasma / Rb) is bounded by hepatic blood flow (Q_H ~ 90 L/h in a 70 kg adult) unless extrahepatic clearance (renal, pulmonary, blood esterase) contributes, and perfusion-limited organ clearance is bounded by cardiac output (~300 L/h). Apparent extravascular clearance (CL/F) without known F, non-hepatic elimination pathways, and catabolically cleared biologics are not comparable to Q_H.
rules.recommendation: Confirm clearance scale (systemic vs apparent CL/F), blood-to-plasma ratio (Rb = C_blood / C_plasma), and primary elimination pathway. Document justification if extrahepatic metabolism or blood hydrolysis explains CL_blood > Q_H.
rules.reference_basis: Physiological reference values for a 70 kg adult human: Davies B, Morris T, 'Physiological parameters in laboratory animals and humans,' Pharmaceutical Research, 1993;10(7):1093-1095 (hepatic blood flow 1450 mL/min = 87 L/h, rounded to 90 L/h); Brown RP, Delp MD, Lindstedt SL, Rhomberg LR, Beliles RP, 'Physiological parameter values for physiologically based pharmacokinetic models,' Toxicology and Industrial Health, 1997;13(4):407-484 (adult cardiac output ~5.0 L/min = 300 L/h). Blood-to-plasma clearance conversion identity: CL_blood = CL_plasma / Rb. Screening tier assignment (WARN > Q_H, HIGH > CO): PharmAgent screening heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Renal clearance (CL_R) compared against total systemic CL, glomerular filtration (fu * GFR), and effective renal plasma flow (Q_R,plasma)
rules.scientific_rationale: By conservation of mass, renal clearance CL_R cannot exceed total systemic clearance CL. Physiologically, passive glomerular filtration is bounded by fu * GFR (~7.5 L/h * fu in a 70 kg adult); values exceeding fu * GFR require active tubular secretion, and total renal plasma clearance is bounded by effective renal plasma flow (~36 L/h in a 70 kg adult).
rules.recommendation: Verify that CL_R <= CL. If CL_R > fu * GFR, document active tubular secretion; if CL_R > Q_R,plasma, inspect unit conversions and blood-to-plasma partitioning.
rules.reference_basis: Mass-balance identity: CL_R <= CL_total. Physiological reference values for a 70 kg adult human: Davies B, Morris T, 'Physiological parameters in laboratory animals and humans,' Pharmaceutical Research, 1993;10(7):1093-1095 (GFR = 125 mL/min = 7.5 L/h; renal blood flow = 1100 mL/min = 66 L/h, corresponding to effective renal plasma flow ~600 mL/min = 36 L/h at hematocrit 0.45).

rules.description: Estimated central compartment volume (Vc) screening for unusual values relative to plasma volume and typical distribution spaces
rules.scientific_rationale: In compartmental PopPK models, Vc is an apparent distribution volume referenced to measured blood or plasma concentration rather than an anatomical organ volume. Estimated systemic Vc below ~0.03 L/kg (~2.1 L in a 70 kg adult, below plasma volume ~0.043 L/kg) or above 20–50 L/kg is an unusual estimated central volume warranting review of units, early-time sampling, or extensive tissue partitioning.
rules.recommendation: Check volume units (L vs mL or L/kg), bioavailability scaling (Vc vs Vc/F), and early post-dose sampling density; document justification if extreme binding or partitioning explains an unusual estimated Vc.
rules.reference_basis: Physiological plasma volume reference (0.043 L/kg = 3.0 L in 70 kg adult): Davies B, Morris T, 'Physiological parameters in laboratory animals and humans,' Pharmaceutical Research, 1993;10(7):1093-1095. Screening thresholds (0.03 L/kg lower floor, 20.0 L/kg WARN, 50.0 L/kg HIGH): PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Steady-state volume (Vss) mammillary compartment-sum identity (Vss = Vc + sum(Vp)) and heuristic magnitude bounds
rules.scientific_rationale: In a mammillary compartmental model with elimination exclusively from the central compartment, steady-state distribution volume satisfies the exact identity Vss = Vc + sum(Vp) (and Vss >= Vc). In non-mammillary or peripheral-elimination models, Vss does not equal Vc + sum(Vp). Heuristic magnitude screening flags systemic Vss < 0.04 L/kg or > 100 L/kg for review.
rules.recommendation: Confirm compartmental structure (mammillary with central elimination vs peripheral elimination). Reconcile Vss with Vc + sum(Vp) when mammillary, or document tissue sequestration if Vss > 100 L/kg.
rules.reference_basis: Mathematical identity Vss = Vc + sum(Vp) for mammillary systems with central elimination: Gibaldi M, Perrier D, Pharmacokinetics, 2nd ed. (New York, NY: Marcel Dekker; 1982), Chapter 2 ('Multicompartment Models'). Physiological fluid spaces (plasma 0.043 L/kg, ECF 0.20 L/kg, TBW 0.60 L/kg): Davies B, Morris T, Pharmaceutical Research, 1993;10(7):1093-1095. Numerical tolerance (+/-5%) and magnitude bounds ([0.04, 100.0] L/kg): PharmAgent screening heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Terminal half-life (t_half = ln(2)/beta) and effective half-life (t_half_eff = ln(2)*Vss/CL) mathematical consistency and heuristic range
rules.scientific_rationale: Terminal elimination half-life (t_half = ln(2)/beta in multi-compartment models, or ln(2)*Vc/CL in 1-compartment models) and effective half-life (t_half_eff = ln(2)*Vss/CL) are distinct quantities in multi-compartment kinetics (t_half_beta > t_half_eff whenever Vp > 0) and must match their respective analytical definitions.
rules.recommendation: Distinguish terminal half-life (t_half) from effective half-life (t_half_eff) and recompute from compartmental parameters using identical time and volume units.
rules.reference_basis: Linear compartmental eigenmode identity: beta = 0.5 * ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4*k10*k21)), t_half_beta = ln(2)/beta, and effective half-life t_half_eff = ln(2)*MRT = ln(2)*Vss/CL: Gibaldi M, Perrier D, Pharmacokinetics, 2nd ed. (New York, NY: Marcel Dekker; 1982), Chapters 1-2; Boxenbaum HG, Battle M, 'Effective half-life in clinical pharmacology,' Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 1995;35(8):763-766. Consistency tolerance (+/-10%) and heuristic range ([0.01, 5000.0] h): PharmAgent screening heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Extravascular first-order absorption rate constant (ka) route/formulation screening and flip-flop identifiability advisory
rules.scientific_rationale: Expected first-order absorption rate constants (ka) depend on route, modality, and formulation release mechanism (immediate-release oral small molecules vs extended-release, depot/long-acting, or subcutaneous lymphatic mAb absorption). Flip-flop kinetics (ka <= terminal elimination rate beta or ke) are not inherently erroneous—they occur legitimately in extended-release, depot, and subcutaneous formulations—but in immediate-release models without IV reference data, ka and ke can exchange labels during estimation.
rules.recommendation: Confirm extravascular route and formulation_release ('immediate_release', 'extended_release', 'depot_or_long_acting'). For immediate-release models with ka <= beta, verify structural identifiability or document absorption-rate-limited disposition.
rules.reference_basis: Flip-flop kinetics theory and structural identifiability: Yanez JA, Remsberg CM, Sayre CL, Forrest ML, Davies NM, 'Flip-flop pharmacokinetics - delivering a reversal of disposition: challenges and opportunities during drug development,' Therapeutic Delivery, 2011;2(5):643-672. Subcutaneous mAb absorption rate range (0.1-0.8 day^-1 ~ 0.004-0.033 h^-1): Dirks NL, Meibohm B, Clinical Pharmacokinetics, 2010;49(10):633-659. Immediate/extended/depot numerical screening cutoffs: PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Allometric body-weight exponent on clearance parameters (CL, Q) screening range
rules.scientific_rationale: Theory-based allometric scaling relates metabolic and physiological flow clearances to body weight with an exponent near 0.75 (typical empirical PopPK range 0.60–0.90). Estimated exponents outside [0.30, 1.20] often reflect narrow weight distributions or collinearity with age/maturation.
rules.recommendation: Inspect body-weight range in the dataset or fix allometric clearance exponent to 0.75 with documented justification if estimated exponent is poorly identified.
rules.reference_basis: Theory-based allometric scaling (exponent 0.75 for clearances): Anderson BJ, Holford NHG, 'Mechanism-based concepts of size and maturity in pharmacokinetics,' Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology, 2008;48:303-332. Screening intervals ([0.60, 0.90] PASS, [0.30, 1.20] WARN): PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Allometric body-weight exponent on volume parameters (Vc, Vp, Vss) screening range
rules.scientific_rationale: Theory-based allometric scaling relates distribution volumes proportionally to body mass with an exponent near 1.0 (typical empirical PopPK range 0.80–1.20). Estimated exponents outside [0.50, 1.50] suggest covariate confounding or sparse sampling.
rules.recommendation: Inspect body-weight covariate distribution or document justification for non-standard volume scaling.
rules.reference_basis: Theory-based allometric scaling (exponent 1.0 for volumes): Anderson BJ, Holford NHG, 'Mechanism-based concepts of size and maturity in pharmacokinetics,' Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology, 2008;48:303-332. Screening intervals ([0.80, 1.20] PASS, [0.50, 1.50] WARN): PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Inter-individual variability (IIV / Omega) magnitude screening and omega^2 vs %CV mathematical consistency
rules.scientific_rationale: For log-normal IIV, %CV = 100 * sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1). When both omega^2 and %CV are reported, they must be mathematically consistent. Very large IIV (> 100% CV warn, > 200% CV high) often indicates unmodeled subpopulations, outlier subjects, or structural/residual model misspecification.
rules.recommendation: Verify omega^2 to %CV conversion formula and inspect eta distributions, shrinkage, and covariates for parameters with IIV > 100% CV.
rules.reference_basis: Exact log-normal variance-to-CV identity: CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1). Regulatory PopPK evaluation context: U.S. FDA, Population Pharmacokinetics: Guidance for Industry (February 2022); EMA CHMP, Guideline on Reporting the Results of Population Pharmacokinetic Analyses, CHMP/EWP/185990/06 (June 2007). Numerical screening cutoffs (100% CV WARN, 200% CV HIGH, +/-5% consistency tolerance): PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Random-effect and residual variance terms (omega^2, sigma^2) must be finite and non-negative (>= 0)
rules.scientific_rationale: Variance of a real-valued random variable is the expectation of a squared deviation and cannot be negative or non-finite.
rules.recommendation: Fix or re-estimate the variance structure; negative variance estimates indicate a failed covariance step or unconstrained parameterization.
rules.reference_basis: Probability theory axiom: Var(X) = E[(X - E[X])^2] >= 0 for any real-valued random variable X.

rules.description: Covariance matrices (Omega, Sigma) must be square, finite, symmetric, and positive semidefinite (PSD)
rules.scientific_rationale: Every valid covariance matrix M satisfies x^T M x >= 0 for all real vectors x, which requires M = M^T and all eigenvalues >= 0.
rules.recommendation: Inspect off-diagonal covariance estimates or switch to a Cholesky / correlation-parameterized block Omega structure.
rules.reference_basis: Linear algebra and probability identity: a real matrix M is a valid covariance matrix if and only if M is symmetric and positive semidefinite (Golub GH, Van Loan CF, Matrix Computations, 4th ed., Baltimore, MD: Johns Hopkins University Press; 2013, Section 4.2). Numerical tolerances (symmetry 1e-8, eigenvalue -1e-9): PharmAgent floating-point tolerance (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Random-effect correlations must satisfy the Cauchy-Schwarz bound |r| <= 1.0 (CRITICAL) and screen for near-collinearity |r| >= 0.95 (WARN)
rules.scientific_rationale: By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, correlation coefficients must lie in [-1, 1]. Correlations with |r| >= 0.95 indicate near-singular Omega blocks and over-parameterized random effects.
rules.recommendation: Reject any model with |r| > 1.0; for |r| >= 0.95, consider shared-eta scaling or a reduced block structure.
rules.reference_basis: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality: |Cov(X, Y)| <= sqrt(Var(X) * Var(Y)), so |r_XY| <= 1. Near-collinearity warning threshold (|r| >= 0.95): PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review); regulatory context: EMA CHMP, Guideline on Reporting the Results of Population Pharmacokinetic Analyses, CHMP/EWP/185990/06 (June 2007).

rules.description: Residual unexplained variability (RUV) must be finite, non-zero across active terms, internally consistent, and within plausible proportional %CV bounds
rules.scientific_rationale: At least one active residual error term must be strictly positive, and reported sigma_var and sd_or_cv must agree. Proportional residual error exceeding 50% CV (WARN) or 100% CV (HIGH) suggests structural misspecification, timing errors, or unmodeled assay/dosing error.
rules.recommendation: Inspect CWRES/IWRES diagnostics, dosing/sampling timestamps, and bioanalytical assay precision.
rules.reference_basis: Variance-to-SD mathematical identity: sigma_var = SD^2. Regulatory residual error diagnostic context: U.S. FDA, Population Pharmacokinetics: Guidance for Industry (February 2022). Proportional RUV magnitude cutoffs (50% CV WARN, 100% CV HIGH): PharmAgent modeling heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) systemic central volume (Vc) compared against intravascular plasma volume (~0.03–0.10 L/kg)
rules.scientific_rationale: IgG monoclonal antibodies (~150 kDa) are restricted primarily to the vascular and interstitial spaces due to large molecular size and hydrophilicity; systemic central volume Vc is typically close to plasma volume (~0.04–0.06 L/kg, ~2.5–4.5 L in a 70 kg adult).
rules.recommendation: Verify mAb Vc units and whether Vc is systemic (IV) or apparent (Vc/F from SC dosing); document justification if target-mediated binding alters apparent Vc.
rules.reference_basis: Published IgG mAb population PK reference range (Vc ~ 2.4-3.2 L in adults, ~0.034-0.046 L/kg): Dirks NL, Meibohm B, 'Population pharmacokinetics of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies,' Clinical Pharmacokinetics, 2010;49(10):633-659. Screening bands ([0.03, 0.10] L/kg PASS, (0.10, 0.15] L/kg WARN, outside HIGH): PharmAgent screening heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Monoclonal antibody (mAb) systemic linear clearance (CL) compared against endogenous IgG catabolic clearance (~0.003–0.05 L/h per 70 kg)
rules.scientific_rationale: Because FcRn recycling protects IgG from lysosomal degradation and intact IgG (~150 kDa) is not filtered by the glomerulus, linear nonspecific mAb clearance is typically ~0.15–0.5 L/day (~0.006–0.021 L/h) in a 70 kg adult unless target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) or anti-drug antibodies (ADA) accelerate clearance.
rules.recommendation: Verify time units (L/day vs L/h; a 24-fold unit error is common in mAb models) and document TMDD or immunogenicity if systemic CL > 0.05 L/h.
rules.reference_basis: Published IgG mAb population PK reference range (linear CL ~ 0.2-0.5 L/day = 0.0083-0.0208 L/h in 70 kg adults): Dirks NL, Meibohm B, 'Population pharmacokinetics of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies,' Clinical Pharmacokinetics, 2010;49(10):633-659. Screening bands ([0.003, 0.05] L/h PASS, (0.05, 0.15] L/h WARN, TMDD cap 1.0 L/h): PharmAgent screening heuristic (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Inter-compartmental clearance (Q, Q2) and micro-rate constants (k12 = Q/Vc, k21 = Q/Vp, k13 = Q2/Vc, k31 = Q2/Vp2, k10 = CL/Vc) identity and cardiac output bound
rules.scientific_rationale: When both micro-rate constants (k12, k21, k13, k31, k10) and clearance/volume parameters (Q, Q2, CL, Vc, Vp, Vp2) are reported, they must satisfy exact algebraic identities (k12 = Q/Vc, k21 = Q/Vp, k10 = CL/Vc), and perfusion-limited inter-compartmental clearance Q cannot exceed cardiac output.
rules.recommendation: Reconcile micro-rate constants with Q, CL, Vc, and Vp, and verify that Q does not exceed scaled cardiac output.
rules.reference_basis: Linear compartmental parameter conversion identities (k10 = CL/Vc, k12 = Q/Vc, k21 = Q/Vp): Gibaldi M, Perrier D, Pharmacokinetics, 2nd ed. (New York, NY: Marcel Dekker; 1982), Chapter 2. Cardiac output reference (300 L/h in 70 kg adult): Brown RP et al., Toxicology and Industrial Health, 1997;13(4):407-484. Relative tolerance (+/-2%): PharmAgent numerical rounding tolerance (pending_owner_review).

rules.description: Predicted concentrations (PRED, IPRED) must be finite, non-negative (>= 0), and within physical mass-concentration limits
rules.scientific_rationale: Drug mass concentration cannot be negative or non-finite (NaN/Inf). Concentrations exceeding 1e6 mg/L (1 kg/L, roughly the density of water) indicate unit mis-scaling or numerical overflow.
rules.recommendation: Reject negative or non-finite predicted concentrations; check ODE solver tolerances, log-transformation, or dose/volume unit scaling.
rules.reference_basis: Physical mass-concentration non-negativity identity (C(t) >= 0) and aqueous solution density ceiling (~1e6 mg/L = 1000 g/L).
